extraction_method: Hedges' g = 0.48 taken directly from the report (Results text, p.481/offset 26159): the covariate-adjusted standardized mean difference favoring MTP-S, derived from the HLM impact (Table 2: MTP-S intervention coefficient B = 14.67**, SE = 5.39, p<.01) standardizing by the within-group/residual SOL SD (~30.56 points, implied by b/g = 14.67/0.48). Small-sample correction J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 1193 gives J = 0.9994, negligible, so g_reported already = g. g_se = J*(SE_b/s) = 0.9994*(5.39/30.56) = 0.176; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.0311 (back-computed; not paper-stated).
page_ref: Results 'Primary Intervention Effects' p.481 (BioC offset 26159) for g=.48/.31; Table 2 (p.482) MTP-S coefficient B=14.67**, SE=5.39; Table 1 (p.482) sample sizes; Figure 1 (means by group).
notes: Single pooled student-achievement contrast (one TPD arm vs. business-as-usual). The report's HEADLINE/confirmatory result is the covariate-adjusted Hedges' g = 0.48 (after covarying individual prior-year SOL score [r=.77 with outcome], grade level, family poverty, racial/ethnic minority status); the SIMPLE unadjusted comparison gave Hedges' g = 0.31 (same contrast, no covariates) -- not extracted as a separate row since it is the same contrast; per spec the covariate-adjusted estimate is preferred. Effect was equivalent to moving the typical student from the 50th to the 59th percentile. Content area (English/history/SS vs. math/science) tested as moderator: NO main or moderating effect (p>.50) -> single pooled effect across subjects, hence outcome_subject='Other'. Clustering: design randomized teachers/classrooms (86 clusters); HLM nested students-within-teachers-within-schools, but preliminary 3-level models found no significant school effects (all p>.35) so the school level was dropped; the teacher/class HLM impact estimate accounts for the relevant nesting -> cluster_adjusted=true. ICC not reported as a single design-effect value (left null per spec; never guess). n_t=659, n_c=536 from Table 1 (male+female counts); paper text rounds total to 1,194 (Table 1 sums to 1,195). Tests are Virginia state SOL end-of-course exams (standardized, independent of developers). Conflict-of-interest note: R. Pianta co-owns the MTP dissemination company.

notes: This is the report's PRIMARY CONFIRMATORY student-achievement contrast: Year-2 schoolwide two-level HLM impact of UD on state math scale score. Treatment effect +0.16 scale points, SE 1.06, z=0.15, p=0.883 -> no overall effect (ES .007). Model controls for prior (SY 2010-11) state math score, race/ethnicity, FRL, ELL, gifted, learning disability, grade, missing-pretest flag, and school block (random school effect). mean_t/mean_c are unadjusted descriptive posttest means (Table 2.6); the +0.16 is the covariate-adjusted impact. EXPLORATORY (not extracted as separate full-sample rows): block-specific Year-2 effects ranged from ES=-.29 (Block 1 lowest-needs, p<.05, significantly NEGATIVE) up to ES=.15 (Block 4 highest-needs, n.s.) (Table 4.6/Fig 4.1, p.56); a streamlined dosage model for students taught 2 yrs by a UD teacher gave ES=.05, p=.04 (Table 4.9, p.61); restricting to ITT teachers' students, Block 4 reached ES=.40, p=.01 (Table 4.12, p.63) -- a non-randomised subgroup, the 'effect size = .40' cited in the Executive Summary. Year-1 student results (a teacher 'learning year') were also exploratory and null overall (schoolwide treatment effect -0.56, p=0.458; Table 4.13, p.64). Teacher outcomes (data use ES .37, attitudes/beliefs ES .34, knowledge/skills ES .25) are NOT student achievement and were not extracted per spec.

SE(d)=SE(b)/s=0.99/15=0.066, Var(d)=0.004356. Hedges' J=1-3/(4*df-1) with df large (~200 teachers/many students) -> J=0.9962, so g=J*d=0.123, Var(g)=J^2*Var(d)=0.004323, SE(g)=0.066. Standardized by the TEMA-3 reference SD because the paper reports no posttest/gain SD and the impact estimate is in TEMA-3 ability-score units.
page_ref: p.147 Table 6 (impact estimate 1.85, SE 0.99, t=1.88, p=.061; variance components); p.145 (TEMA-3 mean 100, SD 15); p.147-148 results text
notes: QED matched-comparison study. Only one student achievement outcome reported (TEMA-3 mathematics). HLM controls for fall math ability score (pretest), SES (building free/reduced lunch %), time, plus teacher-level predictors (Numbers & Operations MKT, Anxiety, Student-Centered Beliefs); model already nests students within teachers so the SE accounts for clustering -> cluster_adjusted=true. Positive g favors Primarily Math. Significant at the study's prespecified alpha=.10 (p=.061) but not at .05. Effect described by authors as 'small but positive,' consistent with g~0.12. Teacher (not student) outcomes (MKT subscales, FSMAS attitudes, MBS beliefs) were NOT extracted per instructions. n_clusters=184 is the count of teachers whose students were tested (Table 1, 80 PM + 104 comparison; K-2 subset ~73+90); student-level Ns not reported. extraction_method: Pretest-adjusted (ANCOVA-style 3-level HLM) impact estimate divided by the student-level pooled within-group posttest SD, exactly as the authors define it (p.~22, line: 'effect size was computed as a standardized mean difference (Hedge's g) by dividing the adjusted group mean difference (gamma010) by the pooled within-intervention and control group standard deviation of the student-level outcome score'). Numerator gamma010 = 0.78 TerraNova scale points (Table 12 bottom row / chapter 4; SE=1.27); standardizing SD = pooled student-level posttest SD = 38.69 (p.41). d = 0.78/38.69 = 0.02016. Hedges' J = 1 - 3/(4*df - 1) with df ~ 2454 (N=2456-2) ~ 0.99969, so g = J*d = 0.02015 ~ 0.02, matching the authors' reported effect size of 0.02. g_se = impact_se / standardizing_SD = 1.27/38.69 = 0.03283; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.001078. This SE is taken from the multilevel-model impact SE, which accounts for student-within-classroom-within-school clustering (cluster_adjusted=true). Adjusted posttest means (Table 12): intervention 648.29, control 647.50 (diff 0.78 after class-mean pretest adjustment); unadjusted posttest means 647.41 vs 646.60 (diff 0.81, SE 2.36). The authors did not report a separate intervention-group posttest SD (control student-level SD=38.18; pooled=38.69), so sd_t is left null.
